Q558.L1t: Everybody Loves Raymond was an American sitcom that ran on CBS for nine seasons beginning in 1996.
Q558.L2t: The show follows a sportswriter named Ray Barone, who lives near his meddling parents and his brother in Long Island, New York.
Q558.L3t: The lead actor shares his first name with the title character and is a stand-up comedian who also co-created the series, and his surname ends in a vowel, like Barone's.
Q558.L4t: The star of the show is the comedian and actor Ray Romano.
Q558.L2f: Everybody Loves Raymond was set in Chicago and centered on a family of police officers, and it aired on NBC in the 1980s.
Q558.L3f: The lead role was played by a famous retired welterweight and middleweight boxing champion who moved into acting after his fighting career ended.
Q558.L4f: The star of the show is the retired boxing champion Sugar Ray Leonard.

Q485.L1t: Major League Baseball gives out several honors each season to recognize standout players in hitting, pitching and defense.
Q485.L2t: The fielding award is given in both the American and National Leagues, with one winner at each position.
Q485.L3t: The award for top fielders is a trophy shaped like a fielder's mitt, made of gold-colored material and sponsored by a glove maker, rather than a vehicle or other prize of monetary value.
Q485.L4t: The best fielder at each position wins the Gold Glove.
Q485.L2f: The fielding award was first handed out in the 1920s, and only the American League gave it for its first fifty years.
Q485.L3f: Fielding award winners are chosen by a vote of fans, and the prize is a valuable vehicle given by the league's main automobile sponsor.
Q485.L4f: The best fielder at each position wins a brand new car.

Q501.L1t: Mobster slang is full of colorful terms, many of which were popularized by crime movies and by stories of organized crime in America.
Q501.L2t: Canaries are small songbirds, and in underworld slang the bird comparison was used for criminals who gave up secrets.
Q501.L3t: In gangster talk, someone who 'sings' reveals secret information about the organization to law enforcement, which is considered the worst betrayal of the code of silence.
Q501.L4t: Singing like a canary means informing on others by talking to the police.
Q501.L2f: The phrase 'sing like a canary' was coined in the 1990s by a television writer, and it was never used by real criminals.
Q501.L3f: In mobster slang, 'singing' refers to a performer's act of copying a famous crooner at a nightclub owned by the mob, and it has nothing to do with sharing information.
Q501.L4f: Singing like a canary means impersonating Sinatra.
